scope: foundation dataset for People & Appointments, charity-dependence analysis, sector expansion and local-authority finance
critical_findings: Charity status and high public-funding dependence are legally distinct questions. Charity Commission RR7 treats independence from the state as a real legal/governance issue rather than defining charity status by a funding-percentage threshold.

England local-authority revenue finance is mixed: central grants, council tax and retained business rates; fees/charges also finance services. In 2026–27 government grants are budgeted at 54.5% excluding reserve appropriations.
Public libraries are a statutory local service under the Public Libraries and Museums Act 1964; other cultural spending may have different legal footing.
Appointment/career records already reveal testable cross-institutional movement (e.g. Tate→RBO; Chichester/Theatr Clwyd→RSC; ENO→Roundhouse), but no PMC conclusion is encoded.
not_yet_safe: No 'real charity' score: dependence metrics remain descriptive.
No full trustee network yet; directors/CEOs/artistic leadership first.
No public-dependence percentage where audited notes have not been reconciled.
No claim that all local cultural spending is funded by central government.
